result:
All three solutions give 16. I checked the upper bound directly: the four sign-matrix determinants in Solutions 1 and 2 satisfy per = ½(±D₁ ± … ) exactly at the monomial level, so k ≤ 16 holds. For the lower bound, I reconstructed an argument that appears to give k ≥ 16, though the write-ups themselves have gaps. Lemma 1 in Solution 2 assumes distinct columns, which isn't required, but the conclusion (at least four terms to express the all-ones vector) still holds. Solution 2 has the most complete argument and a correct explicit construction, which I verified. Solution 1's lower bound is sketchy, and Solution 3 relies on unverifiable computational claims.

CHOICE: 2
